chunks: Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I have taught this son of mine writing; into what occupation should I place him?”

He said: “Entrust him to Allah—may your father be for you—and do not place him in five occupations: do not place him as a seller of shrouds, nor a jeweler, nor a butcher, nor a grain dealer, nor a slave trader.”

He said: “O Messenger of Allah, what is the seller of shrouds?” He said: “The one who sells shrouds and wishes for the death of my Ummah; and a newborn from my Ummah is more beloved to me than all upon which the sun rises.”
“As for the jeweler, he deals in cheating my Ummah; and as for the butcher, he slaughters until mercy departs from his heart.”
“As for the grain dealer, he hoards food against my Ummah; and it is more beloved to me that a servant meet Allah as a thief than that he meet Him having hoarded food for forty days.”
“And as for the slave trader, Jibraʾil عليه السلام came to me and said: ‘O Muhammad, indeed the worst of your Ummah are those who sell people.’”

key_terms.احْتَكَرَ: hoarded goods, especially food, to the harm of others
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: writing or literacy that the son had been taught

ai.seo_question: Which professions did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله discourage for one’s child, and why?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله warning against placing one’s child in certain trades because of the moral harms commonly associated with them, such as wishing for death, cheating people, hardening the heart, hoarding food, and trading in human beings. It emphasizes ethical livelihood, concern for the Ummah, and the spiritual consequences of one’s profession.
